items.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence: set mein sirf run ka start dhoondho
items.spoken_hook: Sort करके solve किया, interviewer बोला O(n) चाहिए!
items.hook_source: Relatable stake: sorted solution rejected in interview; least used hook type of last six
items.one_idea: Longest Consecutive Sequence: put all numbers in a hash set and start counting only from numbers whose x-1 is not in the set, so every number is walked at most once and no sorting is needed.
items.visual_idea: A number line with the array values as filled cells and gaps empty; cells with a filled left neighbour are greyed out, cells with an empty left neighbour get a start flag and a pointer slides right counting while the next cell is filled, with the run length shown. Actual Python code visible in readable chunks synced to the voice.
items.example: EXAMPLE nums = [100, 4, 200, 1, 3, 2]: run starts 1, 100, 200; run from 1 is 1,2,3,4 so the answer is 4. [0,3,7,2,5,8,4,6,0,1] gives 9. Without the skip check on [1..2000] there are 2,001,000 set lookups vs 4,000 with it (EXAMPLE).
facts_to_verify: Problem paraphrased from doocs mirror of LeetCode 128. Hash set average O(1) lookup per Wikipedia/Python FAQ. O(n) time and O(n) extra space is our own derived analysis. Code was run: 4, 9, 0 (qa/d017/run_output.txt). 2 million vs 4 thousand lookups is EXAMPLE arithmetic on [1..2000].

items.title: Subarray Sum Equals K: prefix sum aur hash map se count
items.spoken_hook: Interviewer ने पूछा: कितने subarrays का sum exactly k है, negatives के साथ?
items.hook_source: Interviewer asked: the problem as one complete question; interviewer_asked is the unused hook type of the last six built (d012-d017). No company claim.
items.hook_10s: Interviewer ने पूछा: कितने subarrays का sum exactly k है, negatives के साथ? Subarray यानी array का continuous हिस्सा. [Frame 0: array 3, 4, -3, 2, 1, 1 with a bracket on 4, -3, 2 and the label sum = 3]
items.one_idea: Subarray Sum Equals K: a subarray ending at the current index sums to k exactly when an earlier prefix sum equals current_prefix - k, so keep a hash map of prefix-sum counts and add seen[current - k] at each step; sliding window fails because negatives break monotonic growth.
items.visual_idea: The array as a row of cells with a running prefix-sum strip underneath; at each cell a pointer reads the current prefix, a lookup arrow jumps to a hash-map table of prefix to count and highlights the entry for current minus k, the matching subarray bracket lights on the array and the answer counter rises. A short side panel shows a sliding window on 3, 4, -3, 2, 1, 1 shrinking past a valid subarray and missing it. Actual Python code visible in readable chunks synced to the voice.
items.everyday_anchor: none: audience is working engineers; technical explanation only.
items.example: EXAMPLE nums = [3, 4, -3, 2, 1, 1], k = 3: answer 3 (subarrays [3], [4, -3, 2], [2, 1]). [1, 2, 3] k = 3 gives 2; [1, 1, 1] k = 2 gives 2; [1, -1, 0] k = 0 gives 3. Sliding window on the first array returns 1 (wrong). Brute force for n = 20000 checks 200,010,000 subarrays vs 20,000 steps (EXAMPLE).
items.code_outline: seen = {0: 1}; s = ans = 0; for x in nums: s += x; ans += seen.get(s - k, 0); seen[s] = seen.get(s, 0) + 1; return ans. Query before insert.
facts_to_verify: Problem paraphrased from the doocs mirror of LeetCode 560 (fetched): negatives allowed; prefix-sum + hash-map, seen={0:1}, query before insert, O(n) time and space. Prefix sum definition from Wikipedia.

Code run: 3, 2, 2, 3 for the four examples; 0 mismatches vs brute force on 5000 random arrays; sliding window gave 1 on [3,4,-3,2,1,1] k=3 (true 3). Sliding-window-fails-with-negatives is our own derivation. 200,010,000 vs 20,000 is EXAMPLE arithmetic.

items.title: Majority Element: Boyer-Moore voting, O(1) space mein
items.spoken_hook: Majority Element सिर्फ़ दो variables से, hash map के बिना।
items.hook_source: surprising_fact is the oldest of the last six built (d013-d018). Payoff verified (fetched in this session): doocs 0169 and Wikipedia state O(n) time and O(1) space. No company claim.
items.hook_10s: Majority Element सिर्फ़ दो variables से, hash map के बिना। [Frame 0: array 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2 with CANDIDATE and COUNT boxes and a crossed-out hash map table beside it]
items.one_idea: Majority Element: when a value appears more than n/2 times, keep one candidate and one counter; a different element cancels one vote, and because the majority outnumbers all other elements put together, the candidate left at the end is the majority (Boyer-Moore voting, O(n) time, O(1) space).
items.visual_idea: A row of cells for 2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2 with a CANDIDATE box and a COUNT counter below; each step a ring moves over a cell and the counter ticks up or down, unequal cells cancel in pairs with a connecting line, the candidate box swaps from 2 to 1 and back to 2 when the count hits zero. A short side panel shows the brute-force count table growing. Actual Python code visible in readable chunks synced to the voice.
items.everyday_anchor: none: audience is working engineers; technical explanation only.
items.example: EXAMPLE nums = [2, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2, 2], n = 7: majority is 2 (4 times). Trace (candidate, count): (2,1) (2,2) (2,1) (2,0) (1,1) (1,0) (2,1). [3, 2, 3] gives 3; [1] gives 1; [-1, -1, 5, -1, 7] gives -1. Brute force for n = 50000 does up to 2,500,000,000 comparisons vs 50,000 steps (EXAMPLE).
items.code_outline: m = cnt = 0; for x in nums: if cnt == 0: m, cnt = x, 1 else: cnt += 1 if x == m else -1; return m. Valid only when a majority (> n/2) is guaranteed.
facts_to_verify: doocs LC 169 (fetched): majority appears more than floor(n/2) times, guaranteed; n up to 5 x 10^4; Moore voting O(n) time, O(1) space.
Wikipedia (fetched): candidate/counter rules; O(n) time, O(1) extra space; without a strict majority the result is arbitrary.
Code run in qa/d019/run.py: [2,2,1,1,1,2,2] -> 2; trace as in the example; [1,2,3] -> 3; [3,1,3,2,3] ends (3,1). 2,500,000,000 vs 50,000 is EXAMPLE arithmetic.

items.title: Rotate Array: teen reverse se in-place, O(1) space mein
items.spoken_hook: Rotate Array: slice लिखा, पर array बदला ही नहीं!
items.hook_source: relatable_stake; payoff verified: doocs 189 and run in qa/d020/run.py. No company claim.
items.hook_10s: Rotate Array: slice लिखा, पर array बदला ही नहीं! [Frame 0: row 1..7 and a second rotated row, original stamped NOT CHANGED]
items.one_idea: Rotate Array: rotating right by k means the last k elements move to the front; do it in place by taking k mod n and reversing three times (the whole array, then the first k, then the remaining n - k), which is O(n) time and O(1) extra space, while the slice-and-assign shortcut builds a new list and does not change the caller's array.
items.visual_idea: One row of 7 cells holding 1 to 7. First scene: a code line builds a second, rotated row beside it while the original row stays unchanged under a NOT CHANGED stamp. Then the same row is reversed three times with swap arcs; last k cells (5,6,7) coloured. A side bar compares the extra copy (7 cells) with zero extra cells.
items.code_outline: def rotate(nums, k): n = len(nums); k %= n; reverse(0, n-1); reverse(0, k-1); reverse(k, n-1). Code run in qa/d020/run.py.
facts_to_verify: doocs LC 189 (fetched): reverse whole, then first k, then last n-k; k %= n; O(n) time, O(1) space.
Run in qa/d020/run.py: slice version leaves [1..7] unchanged; steps match; [1,2] k=3 -> [2,1] and without mod IndexError.

items.title: Set Matrix Zeroes: pehli row aur column ko hi marker bana do, O(1) space
items.spoken_hook: Set Matrix Zeroes: extra array के बिना कैसे करें?
items.hook_source: direct_question; least used among the last six built (d015-d020: surprising_fact x2, relatable_stake x2, interviewer_asked x1, direct_question x1 on d015). Payoff verified: doocs 0073 and run in qa/d021/run.py. No company claim.
items.hook_10s: Set Matrix Zeroes: extra array के बिना कैसे करें? Given matrix, एक cell zero हो तो उसकी पूरी row और column zero होनी चाहिए, in place. [Frame 0: 3x4 grid with two zero cells and their rows and columns shaded, a question mark over a second grid labelled EXTRA]

hook_candidates.text: Set Matrix Zeroes: extra array के बिना कैसे करें?
Matrix में एक zero आया, तो पूरी row-column zero. In place कैसे?
Set Matrix Zeroes: pehle zero करते ही पूरा matrix zero क्यों हो गया?

items.one_idea: Set Matrix Zeroes: if a cell is 0, its whole row and column become 0, in place; zeroing while scanning cascades new zeros and wipes the matrix, so first record which rows and columns have a zero, and do it with O(1) extra space by using the first row and first column as the markers, saving two booleans for whether the first row and first column originally had a zero (O(m*n) time).
items.visual_idea: A 3x4 grid of cells. Two zero cells light up their row and column strips. Scene 2: zeroing during the scan turns new cells to 0 and the whole grid goes zero under a WIPED stamp. Scene 3: the top row and left column are tinted as header strips; each interior zero drops a mark arrow onto its row header and column header; two small flag boxes hold the original first row and first column state. Scene 4: pass two zeroes interior cells wherever a header is marked, then the headers last. A side bar compares two extra arrays (m + n cells) with two flags.
items.code_outline: def setZeroes(matrix): m, n = len(matrix), len(matrix[0]); first_row = any(v == 0 for v in matrix[0]); first_col = any(matrix[i][0] == 0 for i in range(m)); pass 1 over i,j >= 1: if matrix[i][j] == 0: matrix[i][0] = matrix[0][j] = 0; pass 2 over i,j >= 1: if matrix[i][0] == 0 or matrix[0][j] == 0: matrix[i][j] = 0; then zero first row if first_row, first column if first_col. Code run in qa/d021/run.py.
facts_to_verify: doocs LC 73 (fetched): array-mark solution O(mn) time, O(m+n) space; in-place marker solution O(mn) time, O(1) space with two flags i0, j0 for the first row and column; constraints 1 <= m, n <= 200.

Run in qa/d021/run.py (planner ran it): marker code matched a brute force on 5000 random matrices; zero-while-scanning version wiped [[0,1,2,0],[3,4,5,2],[1,3,1,5]] to all zeros and was wrong on 425 of 5000; markers without the two flags wrong on 2871 of 5000 (our own check); step counts 16,000,000 vs 80,000 for m = n = 200 are EXAMPLE worst case, our own derivation.
